senses.en: loud, noisy shouting or protest

ex.en: The vociferance of the crowd drowned out the speaker.
ex.zh: 群眾的喧嚷聲淹沒了演講者的聲音。

root.note: 把聲音帶出來、大聲喊 → 喧嚷

senses.en: to shout or cry out loudly, especially in protest

ex.en: Angry fans began to vociferate against the referee's call.
ex.zh: 憤怒的球迷開始大聲抗議裁判的判決。

root.note: 把聲音用力送出 → 大聲叫喊

senses.en: expressing opinions loudly and forcefully
senses.zh: 大聲疾呼的；強烈表達意見的

ex.en: The plan faced vociferous opposition from local parents.
ex.zh: 這項計畫遭到當地家長強烈的反對。

root.note: 大聲把意見帶出來的 → 大聲疾呼的

senses.en: the popular fashion or style at a particular time

ex.en: Wide-leg jeans are back in vogue this year.
ex.zh: 寬褲管牛仔褲今年又流行起來了。

mn: 常用 in vogue（正流行）、out of vogue（退流行）。

senses.en: able to fly; (in heraldry) shown flying
senses.zh: 能飛的；（紋章）呈飛翔姿態的

senses.en: nimble; quick

ex.en: The family crest shows a volant eagle above a golden shield.
ex.zh: 這個家族紋章上有一隻展翅飛翔的老鷹，位於金色盾牌之上。

senses.en: likely to change suddenly and unpredictably, often for the worse
(of a person) prone to sudden anger
(of a substance) easily evaporating

ex.en: Stock prices have been volatile since the election.
ex.zh: 選舉以來股價一直劇烈波動。

root.note: 容易飛走的 → 易揮發、易變的

senses.en: the power of choosing or deciding for oneself

ex.en: She left the company of her own volition; nobody forced her.
ex.zh: 她是自願離開公司的，沒有人逼她。

mn: 常用 of one's own volition（出於自願）。

senses.en: relating to the will; (grammar) expressing a wish or desire
senses.zh: 意志的；（文法）表達願望的

ex.en: "May you be happy" is an example of a volitive sentence.
ex.zh: 「願你幸福」是表達願望句的一個例子。

senses.en: speaking easily, rapidly, and at length

ex.en: The voluble tour guide talked nonstop for two hours.
ex.zh: 那位健談的導遊連續講了兩個小時。

root.note: 話語滾滾而出 → 口若懸河的

senses.en: giving or showing pleasure to the senses; luxurious
senses.zh: 令人感官愉悅的；豐美的

senses.en: (of a woman) having a full, curvy figure

ex.en: The chef served a voluptuous chocolate cake with cream.
ex.zh: 主廚端上一個搭配鮮奶油的濃郁巧克力蛋糕。

senses.en: wanting or eating great quantities of food
very eager in a particular activity

ex.en: She is a voracious reader who finishes three books a week.
ex.zh: 她是個如飢似渴的讀者，一週讀完三本書。

mn: voracious reader（熱愛閱讀的人）是 SAT 常見搭配；carnivore（肉食動物）也有 vor。

senses.en: a mass of whirling fluid or air, such as a whirlpool
a situation that draws people in and is hard to escape

ex.en: The boat was pulled into the vortex of the whirlpool.
ex.zh: 小船被捲進了漩渦中心。

senses.en: a person who has made religious vows, such as a monk or nun
a devoted follower or supporter

ex.en: He became a lifelong votary of classical music.
ex.zh: 他成為古典音樂的終身愛好者。

root.note: 發了誓言的人 → 虔誠的信徒

senses.en: offered to fulfill a vow or as an act of devotion

ex.en: Visitors lit a votive candle at the shrine.
ex.zh: 訪客們在神龕前點了一根祈願蠟燭。

root.note: 為了誓言而獻上的 → 還願的

senses.en: the quality of being rude, crude, or lacking good taste
a rude or offensive word or act

ex.en: The comedian's constant vulgarity offended part of the audience.
ex.zh: 那位喜劇演員滿口粗話，冒犯了部分觀眾。

senses.en: easily harmed or attacked, physically or emotionally

ex.en: Elderly people are especially vulnerable during heat waves.
ex.zh: 熱浪期間，老年人特別容易受到傷害。

root.note: 能被傷害的 → 脆弱的

senses.en: a homeless, neglected, or abandoned person, especially a child
a very thin, delicate-looking person

ex.en: The kind baker gave bread to a hungry waif every morning.
ex.zh: 好心的麵包師傅每天早上送麵包給一個挨餓的流浪兒。

mn: 常見片語 waifs and strays（無家可歸的人和動物）。

senses.en: (British) a sleeveless, buttoned garment worn over a shirt; a vest

ex.en: The groom wore a gray waistcoat under his jacket.
ex.zh: 新郎在西裝外套裡穿了一件灰色背心。

mn: 美式英語多說 vest；舊式英式讀法也有 [ˋwɛskət]。

senses.en: to choose not to demand or enforce a right, claim, or fee

ex.en: The college agreed to waive the application fee for low-income students.
ex.zh: 這所大學同意免除低收入學生的申請費。

mn: 與 wave（揮手）同音，但意思完全不同。

senses.en: small shell beads used by some Native American peoples as money or decoration
senses.zh: 貝殼串珠（北美原住民用作貨幣或飾品）

ex.en: The museum displays a wampum belt that recorded a peace treaty.
ex.zh: 博物館展示一條記錄和平條約的貝殼串珠腰帶。

senses.en: to decrease gradually in strength, power, or importance
(of the moon) to appear smaller each night

ex.en: Public interest in the story began to wane after a week.
ex.zh: 一週後，大眾對這則新聞的興趣開始減退。

mn: wax and wane（盈虧、興衰）是固定搭配。

senses.en: deliberate, needless cruelty or destruction
(old use) sexual immorality

ex.en: The wantonness of the vandals shocked the neighborhood.
ex.zh: 那些破壞者的肆意妄為讓整個社區震驚。

root.note: 不受約束的狀態 → 肆意妄為

senses.en: hostile and eager to fight
relating to war

ex.en: The ancient Spartans were known as a warlike people.
ex.zh: 古斯巴達人以好戰聞名。

root.note: 像要打仗的 → 好戰的

senses.en: a small wave; a ripple
(mathematics) a function used in signal processing

ex.en: Each wavelet lapped softly against the side of the canoe.
ex.zh: 每一道小波浪都輕輕拍打著獨木舟的船身。

senses.en: lacking courage or determination; easily frightened
senses.zh: 軟弱的；膽小的；沒骨氣的

senses.en: weak in the legs from fear or emotion

ex.en: The weak-kneed committee gave in to every demand.
ex.zh: 那個軟弱的委員會對每項要求都讓步了。

senses.en: (formal) well-being; prosperity
a raised red mark on the skin caused by a blow

ex.en: Leaders must act for the public weal, not their own gain.
ex.zh: 領導者必須為公眾福祉而非個人利益而行動。

mn: 固定搭配 in weal and woe（無論禍福）；common weal（公共福利）即 commonwealth 的來源。

senses.en: to stop feeding a baby or young animal with its mother's milk
to make someone gradually stop depending on something

ex.en: The country is trying to wean itself off fossil fuels.
ex.zh: 這個國家正試圖逐步擺脫對化石燃料的依賴。

senses.en: causing tiredness or boredom
senses.zh: 令人厭倦的；使人疲倦的

ex.en: The long, wearisome meeting finally ended at nine.
ex.zh: 這場冗長又令人厭倦的會議終於在九點結束。

senses.en: (chiefly Scottish) very small; tiny
senses.zh: （蘇格蘭用語）很小的；一點點的

senses.en: very early (as in the wee hours)

ex.en: We stayed up talking until the wee hours of the morning.
ex.zh: 我們一直聊到凌晨時分。

mn: the wee hours（凌晨一兩點左右）是常見說法。

senses.en: having good manners, often from a good upbringing
(of an animal) from good breeding stock

ex.en: The well-bred young man stood up whenever a guest entered.
ex.zh: 那位有教養的年輕人每當有客人進來就起身致意。

senses.en: a person who does good deeds

ex.en: The town honored the well-doer who secretly paid for the new library.
ex.zh: 鎮上表揚了那位暗中出資蓋新圖書館的善心人士。

senses.en: wealthy; prosperous

ex.en: She grew up in a well-to-do family but chose to work as a teacher in rural areas.
ex.zh: 她生長在富裕家庭，卻選擇到偏鄉當老師。

senses.en: the place where someone or something is
approximately where

ex.en: The whereabouts of the missing painting remain unknown.
ex.zh: 那幅失蹤畫作的下落至今不明。

senses.en: immediately after which

ex.en: The bell rang, whereupon the students rushed out of the classroom.
ex.zh: 鐘聲一響，學生們隨即衝出教室。

senses.en: in or to whatever place
senses.zh: 無論在哪裡；無論到哪裡

senses.en: used for emphasis in questions: where

ex.en: My dog follows me wherever I go.
ex.zh: 我走到哪裡，我的狗就跟到哪裡。

senses.en: (formal, old use) with which; by means of which
(old use) that with which

ex.en: They lacked the tools wherewith to repair the ship.
ex.zh: 他們缺少用來修船的工具。

mn: 現代多用 wherewithal（所需的財力、資源）。

senses.en: to sharpen a blade
to stimulate or increase a desire or interest

ex.en: The movie trailer is designed to whet your appetite for the full film.
ex.zh: 電影預告片就是要勾起你看正片的慾望。

mn: whet one's appetite（引起胃口、激發興趣）是固定搭配。

senses.en: playfully quaint or fanciful in an amusing way
senses.zh: 異想天開的；古靈精怪的

senses.en: acting or changing unpredictably

ex.en: The children's book is full of whimsical drawings of talking animals.
ex.zh: 這本童書充滿會說話的動物的奇趣插畫。

senses.en: to complain in a feeble or annoying way
to make a long, high-pitched cry

ex.en: Please don't whine about the homework; just start it.
ex.zh: 別再抱怨作業了，開始寫就對了。

senses.en: entirely; fully

ex.en: I wholly agree with your decision to study abroad.
ex.zh: 我完全贊同你出國念書的決定。

mn: 與 holy（神聖的）同音，但 wholly = whole + ly。

senses.en: to hold and use a weapon or tool
to have and use power or influence

ex.en: Social media companies wield enormous influence over public opinion.
ex.zh: 社群媒體公司對輿論擁有巨大的影響力。

senses.en: a clever trick used to deceive or persuade (usually plural)
to lure or entice

ex.en: The fox used every wile it knew to get into the henhouse.
ex.zh: 狐狸使出渾身解數想溜進雞舍。

mn: wily（狡猾的）就是 wile 的形容詞；別和 while 搞混。

senses.en: attractive or appealing in a charming, innocent way

ex.en: The little girl gave the photographer a winsome smile.
ex.zh: 小女孩對攝影師露出一個討喜的笑容。

mn: win（贏得）+ some：能贏得人心的 → 迷人的。

senses.en: typical of winter; cold, snowy, or icy
(of a manner) cold and unfriendly

ex.en: Wintry weather closed several mountain roads this weekend.
ex.zh: 這週末嚴寒的天氣封閉了幾條山路。

senses.en: lean, tough, and strong
(of hair) stiff and coarse like wire

ex.en: The wiry marathon runner looked thin but had amazing endurance.
ex.zh: 那位精瘦結實的馬拉松跑者看起來瘦，耐力卻驚人。

root.note: 像鐵絲一樣細而硬韌的

senses.en: the practice of magic, especially to cause harm

ex.en: In the 1600s, many innocent people were accused of witchcraft.
ex.zh: 在十七世紀，許多無辜的人被指控施行巫術。

senses.en: foolish; stupid
(as in scared witless) extremely, to the point of losing one's wits

ex.en: The thunderstorm scared the puppy witless.
ex.zh: 雷雨把小狗嚇得魂飛魄散。

root.note: 沒有智力的 → 愚蠢的

senses.en: a person who tries to be witty but is not
senses.zh: 自以為風趣的人；小聰明的人

ex.en: The witling at the party kept telling jokes that nobody laughed at.
ex.zh: 派對上那個自以為幽默的人一直講沒人笑的笑話。

senses.en: a witty remark

ex.en: Her clever witticism made the whole table laugh.
ex.zh: 她一句機智的妙語讓整桌人都笑了。

senses.en: deliberately; with full awareness

ex.en: She would never wittingly hurt anyone's feelings.
ex.zh: 她絕不會故意傷害任何人的感情。

mn: 反義字 unwittingly（不知不覺地）更常見。

senses.en: to shrivel or wrinkle with age
shriveled; wrinkled

ex.en: Apples left too long in the sun will wizen and lose their juice.
ex.zh: 蘋果在太陽底下放太久會乾癟、失去水分。

mn: 形容詞通常用 wizened（乾癟的）。

senses.en: having a thin, shriveled, and wrinkled face
senses.zh: 面容乾癟的；滿臉皺紋的

ex.en: A wizen-faced old man sold chestnuts on the corner.
ex.zh: 一位滿臉皺紋的老人在街角賣栗子。

senses.en: a man who works for wages, especially in manual or industrial labor

ex.en: The new law was meant to protect the working-man from unsafe factories.
ex.zh: 新法旨在保護勞工免於不安全的工廠環境。

mn: 現代多拼作 workingman 或 working man。

senses.en: showing competent, efficient skill, but not brilliant
senses.zh: 工整熟練的；稱職但不出色的

ex.en: The team gave a workmanlike performance and won by one goal.
ex.zh: 這支隊伍表現中規中矩，以一球之差獲勝。

root.note: 像熟練工人那樣的 → 稱職的

senses.en: the skill with which something is made, and the quality that results

ex.en: The fine workmanship of the antique table impressed the buyers.
ex.zh: 這張古董桌的精湛做工讓買家印象深刻。

senses.en: to argue in a long, complicated, or angry way
a long, complicated dispute
to round up or herd livestock

ex.en: The two sides continue to wrangle over the terms of the contract.
ex.zh: 雙方仍在為合約條款爭論不休。

senses.en: to cause a large amount of damage or harm
to inflict revenge

ex.en: The typhoon could wreak havoc on the island's farms.
ex.zh: 颱風可能對島上的農田造成嚴重破壞。

mn: 固定搭配 wreak havoc（造成大混亂）；別和 wreck 混淆。

senses.en: to pull something away from someone with force
to take power or control after great effort

ex.en: The rebels tried to wrest control of the capital from the army.
ex.zh: 叛軍試圖從軍隊手中奪取首都的控制權。

mn: wrestle（摔角）就是 wrest 的延伸。

senses.en: a state of great unhappiness or misery
very poor quality or condition

ex.en: The novel depicts the wretchedness of life in the city's slums.
ex.zh: 這部小說描寫都市貧民窟生活的悲慘。

senses.en: to twist and squirm, as from pain
to suffer great emotional discomfort

ex.en: The injured player began to writhe on the grass in pain.
ex.zh: 受傷的球員痛得在草地上翻滾。

senses.en: the activity or skill of writing
written work, especially of a particular author
handwriting

ex.en: Good writing takes practice, patience, and careful revision.
ex.zh: 好的寫作需要練習、耐心和仔細的修改。

senses.en: using or showing dry, mocking humor
(of a face) twisted to show disgust or displeasure

ex.en: He gave a wry smile when he heard his flight was delayed again.
ex.zh: 聽到班機又延誤，他露出一抹苦笑。

senses.en: an animal, especially a horse, that is one year old
senses.zh: 一歲的動物（尤指一歲馬）

senses.en: one year old

ex.en: The farmer sold the yearling at the autumn horse auction.
ex.zh: 農夫在秋季馬匹拍賣會上賣掉了那匹一歲馬。

senses.en: a person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuing their beliefs

ex.en: The fitness zealot refused to skip a single workout, even on holidays.
ex.zh: 那個健身狂即使放假也不肯少練一次。

root.note: 熱忱過頭的人 → 狂熱分子

mn: zeal 唸 [zil]，但 zealot 唸 [ˋzɛlət]，母音不同。

senses.en: the general mood, ideas, and beliefs of a particular period of history

ex.en: The song perfectly captured the zeitgeist of the 1960s.
ex.zh: 這首歌完美捕捉了 1960 年代的時代精神。

senses.en: the time at which something is most powerful or successful; peak
the point in the sky directly overhead

ex.en: The empire reached its zenith under its third ruler.
ex.zh: 這個帝國在第三任統治者時期達到鼎盛。

mn: 反義字 nadir（最低點）常一起考。

senses.en: (literary) a soft, gentle breeze

ex.en: A warm zephyr carried the scent of flowers across the garden.
ex.zh: 一陣暖和的微風把花香吹過整座花園。

root.note: 西風之神帶來和煦的西風 → 微風

senses.en: a belt of the sky divided into twelve signs, each named after a constellation
the Chinese system of twelve animal years

ex.en: Each year in the Chinese zodiac is linked to one of twelve animals.
ex.zh: 中國十二生肖中，每一年都對應十二種動物之一。

root.note: 動物組成的圈 → 黃道帶（多數星座以動物命名）
